prompt:
Research what the Python Software Foundation or the CPython developers have officially said about the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build. Cite the PEP or documentation page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Based on my search, I can provide the following official statements from the Python Software Foundation and CPython developers regarding the performance impact of the free-threaded (no-GIL) build.

**From Official Documentation (Python 3.14.5):**
The documentation explicitly confirms a performance overhead for the free-threaded build and provides specific figures from the pyperformance benchmark suite.

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build has additional overhead when executing Python code compared to the default GIL-enabled build. The amount of overhead depends on the workload and hardware. On the pyperformance benchmark suite, the average overhead ranges from about 1% on macOS aarch64 to 8% on x86-64 Linux systems." | CLAIM: The free-threaded build is slower than the GIL-enabled build, with overhead varying by platform.

SOURCE: https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html | QUOTE: "The free-threaded build will typically use more memory compared to the default build." | CLAIM: The free-threaded build has increased memory usage.

**From PEP 779 (Criteria for Supported Status):**
This PEP, which outlines the criteria for the free-threaded build to become officially supported, gives more detailed performance and memory targets.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "the performance penalty on linear performance, comparing a free-threaded build against a with-GIL build, as measured by the pyperformance benchmarks... is currently around 10% (except on macOS, where it’s more like 3%)." | CLAIM: The current performance penalty for the free-threaded build is around 10% on most platforms, but lower on macOS.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "free-threaded Python currently sees about 15-20% higher memory use (geometric mean, as measured by pyperformance)." | CLAIM: The free-threaded build currently uses 15-20% more memory.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0779/ | QUOTE: "for phase II (not the default flip), we propose 15% as a hard performance target." | CLAIM: The developers propose a maximum acceptable performance penalty of 15% for the officially supported (but not yet default) free-threaded build.

**From Steering Council Discussion on PEP 703 Acceptance:**
The Steering Council, which accepted PEP 703, commented on the expected performance trade-offs.

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "At this point we’re expecting a (worst case) performance penalty of 10-15%." | CLAIM: The Steering Council expected a performance penalty in the range of 10-15%.

SOURCE: https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-703-making-the-global-interpreter-lock-optional-in-cpython-acceptance/37075?u=hugovk | QUOTE: "The performance impact should be isolated to a free-threaded build; a GIL build should not see any performance impact in existing code." | CLAIM: The performance penalty is only for the free-threaded build; the standard GIL-enabled build is unaffected.

**Regarding PEP 703 itself:**
The original PEP 703 also provided specific performance measurements.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "The changes to make CPython thread-safe without the GIL increase execution overhead for `--disable-gil` builds." | CLAIM: Acknowledges that the no-GIL build incurs a performance overhead.

SOURCE: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/ | QUOTE: "One thread | 6% | 5%" and "Multiple threads | 8% | 7%" | CLAIM: Provided specific overhead figures for single-threaded (5-6%) and multi-threaded (7-8%) execution on different CPU architectures.

In summary, the official sources uniformly state that the free-threaded build currently incurs a performance overhead and uses more memory compared to the standard build, but they consider this an acceptable trade-off for the benefit of true parallelism.
